column3: DSP nanoparticles for treating nitrogen mustard induced corneal injury
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEThe goal of this project is to evaluate a new method by the subconjunctival injection of DSP nanoparticles fortreating nitrogen mustard (NM)-induced corneal injury. Therapeutic interventions to treat NM-induced ocularinjury has not been identified yet which highlights the need to develop new treatment options for vesicants-induced corneal injury. The sustained releasing DSP-PLA-NP could be effective in preventing corneal NVcorneal ulceration corneal opacity suppressing inflammatory and angiogenic markers after NM exposure.

column3: Multifunctional Biodegradable Zwitterionic Polymer-Drug Conjugates for Multidrug Co-Delivery
column4: Project NarrativeThe applicability of polymer-based drug delivery systems (DDSs) has been significantly restricted by criticaltechnological challenges such as the undesired immunogenicity of polyethylene glycol (PEG) broadly used inDDSs the lack of PEG alternatives with optimal comprehensive properties the scarcity of clinically valid DDSsfor combination therapy and the deficient understanding on topological effects of polymer scaffolds. To addressthese challenges we aim to develop multifunctional biodegradable zwitterionic polymer-drug conjugates(ZPDCs) as novel PEG-free multidrug co-delivery systems with favorable biomedically relevant properties. Alibrary of ZPDCs with different main-chain topology and other structural features will be prepared and theirstructure-dependent biointerface properties will be systematically investigated through biochemical cellular andin vivo studies.

column3: Mechanisms and protective efficacy of nanovaccines against Chlamydia trachomatis
column4: PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE: Chlamydia trachomatis is a sexually transmitted bacterium of public health concerns because it causes morbidity and socioeconomic burdens such as infertility and ectopic pregnancy. There is no vaccine against this pathogen. We have developed two novel C. trachomatis nanovaccines which triggered correlative Th1 protective immune responses in mice. We propose to investigate the mechanisms by which Th1 immune responses are induced and whether the induced responses can provide complete protective immunity against C. trachomatis infection in mice. Achieving this proposal's goals would positively impact C. trachomatis vaccine research and improve our efforts toward developing an anti-Chlamydia vaccine.
